request.content: You are a helpful assistant that translates programming worked examples into other natural languages, maintaining both technical accuracy and the original code formatting.

[[TASK-DEFINITION]] You will be given a worked example. Your job is to translate the [[WORKED-EXAMPLE]] according to the [[TASK-INSTRUCTIONS]]. [[WORKED-EXAMPLE]] [[PROGRAM-NAME]] Repeating Characters of a String (Case 1) [[PROGRAM-DESCRIPTION]] Construct a program that has a function that receives a string and creates a new string that has each character of the given string repeated two times.\nFor example, the new string that will be formed from the string 'abc' is 'aabbcc'. [[SOURCE-CODE]] [[LINE01]] #Step 1: Define the function [[LINE02]] def double_char(s): [[LINE03]] #Step 1.1: Assign initial value to the variable that we need for the new string [[LINE04]] new_s = "" [[LINE05]] #Step 1.2: Iterate through the characters in the given string [[LINE06]] for char in s: [[LINE07]] #Step 1.2.1: Add the repeated character to the the new string [[LINE08]] new_s += char * 2 [[LINE09]] #String 1.3: Print the new string [[LINE10]] print(new_s) [[LINE11]] #Step 2: Call the function [[LINE12]] double_char("Hi There") [[LINE-EXPLANATIONS]] [[LINE02.EXPL1]] We need to first declare the function that receives a string and creates a new string that has each character of the given string repeated two times. The given string is referred by variable s.

Note that all statements following the header line are indented. [[LINE04.EXPL1]] This statement sets variable new_s to the empty string. Later, we will update the content of this variable as we iterate through the characters in the given string. [[LINE06.EXPL1]] We want to iterate over the characters in the given string and add each character repeated two times to the new string. We can use a for loop to iterate through the characters in the given string. [[LINE06.EXPL2]] This for loop assigns the name char to each of the characters in the given string in turn, from left to right, and then the statement in the loop body will be executed for each character. [[LINE06.EXPL3]] Note that all statements inside the loop need to be indented with respect to the loop header. [[LINE08.EXPL1]] This statement concatenates the string value stored in variable new_s with the character of the given string repeated two times. The result of the concatenation is stored in variable new_s. [[LINE08.EXPL2]] The repetition operator * repeats the character stored in variable char for the specified number of times. Also, note that the + operator creates a new string from the contents of its operands joined. [[LINE08.EXPL3]] The += operator concatenates the string value stored in variable new_s with the character stored in variable char repeated two times and the result is stored in the variable new_s. Thus, this statement is equivalent to the statement new_s = new_s + char * 2. [[LINE10.EXPL1]] This statement prints to the default standard output stream the new string that is stored in variable new_s. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end. [[LINE12.EXPL1]] This statement calls the double_char function and passes the string "Hi There" as its argument. Note that the function call must be done after the function is declared. Be sure to specifically translate the sections labeled [[PROGRAM-NAME]], [[PROGRAM-DESCRIPTION]], [[SOURCE-CODE]], [[LINE-EXPLANATIONS]], and [[LINE-DISTRACTORS]]. In the [[SOURCE-CODE]] section, translate ONLY user-defined string-literals and comments; make sure they are ASCII-folded (i.e., remove any accents or non-ASCII characters).
